flashcards.q: What are the three ways to run Spark on EMR, and the one-line selection heuristic for each?
flashcards.a: EMR on EC2 (full control, best for steady/long-running/custom-tuned workloads), EMR Serverless (AWS manages workers per job, wins below ~70% on-demand cluster utilization), EMR on EKS (Spark as K8s pods, wins when Kubernetes is already the org's standard platform).

flashcards.q: Why must core nodes never run on Spot instances?
flashcards.a: Core nodes run the HDFS DataNode daemon and hold real data replicas. Spot reclamation risks losing those replicas (data loss) and forces an expensive HDFS rebalance across remaining core nodes; losing enough core nodes concurrently can put the NameNode into safe mode, making the whole cluster unusable, not just one job.

flashcards.q: What does a task node run, and why is it safe to put on Spot?
flashcards.a: Only the YARN NodeManager, no HDFS DataNode, no persisted state. Losing a task node to Spot reclamation only loses in-flight compute, which YARN simply reschedules elsewhere.

flashcards.q: What is command-runner.jar and is it Spark-specific?
flashcards.a: A generic AWS-provided wrapper that execs a given command as an EMR step (e.g. spark-submit). Not Spark-specific — the same mechanism runs Hive, Pig, or arbitrary shell commands as steps.

flashcards.q: Why is pip install inside a bootstrap action fragile, specifically?
flashcards.a: It performs live dependency resolution and network calls against external package indices on every single cluster launch, on every node. Any transient network failure, mirror outage, or yanked package version fails the entire cluster launch, and unpinned transitive dependencies can drift between launches even with an identical script.

flashcards.q: What is the venv-pack packaging approach and what flag ships it to executors?
flashcards.a: Build a virtualenv once (e.g. in CI, pinned versions), pack it into one tarball with venv-pack, upload to S3. Ship it via --archives s3://.../env.tar.gz#environment on spark-submit, with PYSPARK_PYTHON=./environment/bin/python. Zero network calls at cluster-launch time.

flashcards.q: What is the default Spot allocation strategy since EMR 6.9.0, and what does it balance?
flashcards.a: price-capacity-optimized. It diversifies across multiple pools that are simultaneously low-priced AND have deep capacity availability, balancing price and interruption risk, rather than optimizing purely for one (lowest-price) or the other (capacity-optimized).

flashcards.q: In what order should you read EMR's step logs when debugging a failure, and why that order?
flashcards.a: 1) Controller log — catches step-launch-level failures (bad args, missing archive, IAM issues) before assuming an app bug. 2) stderr — the actual Spark/JVM stack trace for real application failures. 3) stdout — the app's own status output. 4) YARN per-container logs — one level below the step summary, for individual task/executor-level detail (a specific OOM or exception).

flashcards.q: What is EMR Serverless pre-initialized capacity (initialCapacity), and what's its cost tradeoff?
flashcards.a: A configurable pool of pre-warmed workers a job can draw from immediately instead of provisioning cold. Tradeoff: you pay for those workers continuously even when idle — size it only to the latency-sensitive fraction of traffic, not the whole workload.

flashcards.q: What's the rough EMR pricing model on top of EC2?
flashcards.a: Per-second billing (roughly 1-minute minimum) for both EC2 and the EMR management surcharge; the EMR surcharge itself is roughly an additional ~20% on top of the underlying EC2 instance cost, varying by instance family.

flashcards.q: What changed in EMR release 7.10.0 regarding the S3 connector, and what does it ship for Spark?
flashcards.a: S3A replaced EMRFS as the default S3 connector starting in EMR 7.10.0. That release ships Spark 3.5.5-amzn-1.

flashcards.q: When does a custom AMI pay off over a bootstrap action, and what's the tradeoff?
flashcards.a: Once you run frequent jobs with a stable dependency set — startup is faster and deterministic (no live install at launch), but you now own an image build/publish pipeline (Packer/EC2 Image Builder) and must rebuild whenever dependencies change.

flashcards.q: What utilization threshold makes EMR Serverless cheaper than an on-demand EMR on EC2 cluster, and how does a Savings Plan change that threshold?
flashcards.a: Below roughly 70% on-demand cluster utilization, Serverless is cheaper. Versus a cluster covered by an EC2 Savings Plan, the break-even drops to roughly 50% utilization.
